scope: Mains 4: RBI primary-institutional exchange-rate reform chronology; bounded evidence audit

sources.finding: 1 and 3 July 1991 two-stage rupee devaluation; March 1992 LERMS dual exchange-rate system; 1993 unified exchange rate
LERMS March 1992: 40 percent converted at official RBI rate and 60 percent at market rate; unified market-determined exchange rate effective 1 March 1993; current-account convertibility August 1994
FEMA 1999 replaced FERA and commenced 1 June 2000; unified exchange rate March 1993

verified_claims.claim: Rupee adjusted downward in two stages on 1 and 3 July 1991
LERMS split conversion 40 percent official and 60 percent market
Unified market-determined exchange rate effective 1 March 1993
FEMA became effective 1 June 2000, not during 1991 reform

student_wording: The external-sector reform sequence was the two-stage rupee adjustment (July 1991), dual-rate LERMS (March 1992; 40% official/60% market conversion), unified market-determined exchange rate (1 March 1993), and current-account convertibility (August 1994). The separate FERA-to-FEMA legal transition took effect on 1 June 2000.
limitations: RBI institutional historical material examined, not the original 1991/1992/1993 policy notifications or contemporaneous circulars
Not a line-by-line audit of the actual six mains answers; no claim that existing Mains 4 text contains an error
1991 original Industrial Policy PDF, sectoral employment outcomes and all other mains claims remain unchecked
No manuscript or PDF changes; no independent academic reviewer; no R1-R8 gate promotion
